title: Levetiracetam — Pediatric Status Epilepticus (Second-Line)
sources: Chamberlain JM, et al. ESETT — Trial of Three Anticonvulsant Medications for Status Epilepticus. NEJM. 2019;381:2103-2113.
Glauser T, et al. Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults — AES 2016.
Drug_Dosing_Peds_Weight_Based_Spec.md (cross-checked vs Stanford & Riley Children's pathways).

changelog.change: Initial entry — one of the second/third-line agents named in peds-lorazepam-status's buildNote as the still-needed remainder of the status-epilepticus set.

purpose: Second-line agent for pediatric status epilepticus persisting after an adequate benzodiazepine dose — roughly equivalent efficacy to fosphenytoin and valproate per ESETT, with the most favorable safety/interaction profile of the three, which is moving it earlier in many institutional protocols.

doses.notes: Infuse over ~10 minutes (the ESETT protocol infusion time). No cardiac monitoring requirement — the main practical advantage over fosphenytoin. Renal-dose down-titrate for maintenance dosing, not the acute load.

contraindications: Caution (not an absolute contraindication) in patients with a history of significant behavioral/psychiatric side effects on levetiracetam
buildNote: Second/third-line status-epilepticus sibling of peds-lorazepam-status and peds-midazolam-status. ESETT (2019) found levetiracetam, fosphenytoin (see peds-fosphenytoin-status), and valproate (see peds-valproate-status) roughly equivalent in efficacy (~45-50% seizure cessation) and safety when benzodiazepines fail — choice is largely institutional preference and contraindication profile, not a clear winner.
